t: Mitanni was a Late Bronze Age great power in northern Syria, with a Hurrian population and kings bearing Indo-Aryan names.
Famed for chariot warfare, it rivalled and later allied with Egypt, sealing ties through royal marriages and letters.
A murdered king and contested succession let the Hittites and Assyria carve it up; Assyria annexed the remnant by c. 1250 BCE.
dyk: A Mitanni treaty with the Hittites calls on the gods Mitra, Varuna, Indra and the Nasatyas, some of the earliest evidence for Indo-Aryan languages anywhere.
ev: Barattarna extends Mitanni authority over Aleppo and Alalakh
Shaushtatar sacks Ashur and rules vassals such as Arrapha
Hittite king Suppiluliuma I sacks the capital, Washukanni
The Shattiwaza treaty makes Mitanni a Hittite vassal
Shalmaneser I of Assyria crushes Shattuara II and annexes Hanigalbat
